senses.gloss: what? which? Ḥull. 89ᵃ (play on הא̇מ̇נ̇ם א̇ל̇ם̇, Ps. LVIII, 2) מה א̇ומ̇נ̇תו … כא̇ל̇ם̇ which is the best policy for man in this world? Let him act as if he were mute (keep silence).
units: <cite ref="Bava Metzia 63a:6">B. Mets. 63ᵃ</cite>, a. e. <he>מה לו הן מה לי דמיהן</he> what are they to me and what their equivalent, i.e. what difference does it make whether the purchased objects or their equivalent be delivered?; <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Yoma 5:6:11">Y. Yoma V, 43ᵃ</cite> bot. <he>מה ביניהן ומה בין דמיהן</he>.

B. Bath. 32ᵇ; 31ᵃ מה (לי) לו לשקר what motive could he have to tell a lie? Ib., a. e. מה לי לשקר במקום עדים וכ׳ we do not apply the principle that we believe a defendant because he has no motive to lie, where witnesses are on hand; a. v. fr.—מה … אף what …?, even so, i.e. as … so.
Gitt. 23ᵇ מה אתם … אף וכ׳ as you (Num. XVIII, 28) refers to Israelites, so must your delegate be an Israelite.

Sabb. 133ᵇ מה הוא … אף וכ׳ as He is gracious and merciful, so be thou &c.; a. fr.—מה … לא כל שכן, v. כָּל.—מה … אינו דין, v. דִּין II.—מה ל־ … שכן … תאמר what has this to do with …? In this case …, whereas &c., i.e. it is different with … because &c.

Kidd. 4ᵇ מה ליבמה שכן … תאמר וכ׳ the case of a Y’bamah is different, because she can neither be acquired by means of a document, whereas this (an ordinary woman) &c.; a. fr.—מָה נַפְשְׁךָ (in Babli mostly: מִמָּה נפשך; abbr. ממ״נ) whatever be thy opinion (from whatever opinion thou start), i.e. whichever side you take, at all events.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 1:1:8">Y. Ber. I, 2ᵇ</cite> <he>מ׳ נ׳ אם וכ׳</he> at all events (he has offended); if it was day-time when the first stars (on Friday evening) were visible, it was day-time when the first stars (on Sabbath evening) were visible &c.; <cite ref="Shabbat 35b:3">Sabb. 35ᵇ</cite> <he>חייכ חטאת ממ״נ</he> must bring a sin-offering at all events (whether you consider twilight a part of the day or a part of the night).
<cite ref="Shabbat 34a:10">Ib. 34ᵃ</cite> (in Chald. dict.) <he>מה נפשך אי וכ׳</he> whichever side you take, if twilight is day &c.

<cite ref="Eruvin 10a:3-4">Erub. 10ᵃ</cite> <he>גדולה … למה לי ממ״נ אי וכ׳</he> what reason was there for saying ‘large …’? In either case (it is incorrect), if it be to permit the use of the larger court &c.

<cite ref="Chullin 29a:2">Ḥull. 29ᵃ</cite> <he>ממ״נ אי מחצה וכ׳</he> in either case (the slaughtering is ritually correct); if you adopt the opinion that an exact half is to be considered as if it were the larger portion &c.; a. v. fr.—

senses.gloss: wherewith? B. Bath. 10ᵇ במה תרום וכ׳ whereby can the horn of Israel be lifted up? Sabb. II, 1; a. fr.—
senses.label: a

senses.gloss: in what case? במה דברים אמורים (abbr. בד״א), v. אָמַר I.—לָמָּה wherefore? Ber. 3ᵃ תחלת … סימנא למה לי what need is there for a sign for the beginning of the first watch? M. Kat. 28ᵃ ל׳ נסמכה וכ׳ why is the account of the death of Miriam attached to &c.?; a. fr.—לַמֶּה to what?, whereto? Kidd. 40ᵇ ל׳ צדיקים נמשלים what are the righteous to be compared to?—ל׳ הדבר דומה, v. דָּמָה; a. fr.—V. לָמָה.
